settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted causal bandit on no-backdoor graphs (simple regret)
unmapped: Arms are 2M+1 interventions do(X_i=x) on binary nodes plus the observational arm do(); no backdoor paths from intervenable nodes to reward, so E[Y|do(X_i=x)]=E[Y|X_i=x]
Observational arm reveals sampled values of all X_i (causal side information)
Interventions cost gamma>=1 (known), observation costs 1; total budget B
Known causal graph; X_i ~ Bernoulli(p_i) with unknown p_i and p = min p_{i,x} > 0
settings.definition_quote: We study the budgeted causal bandit problem for no-backdoor graphs. As stated in Section 2, an algorithm for this problem is given as input the graph G, the set of intervenable nodes {X_1, ..., X_M}, a budget B, and gamma which is the cost for pulling an arm a_{i,x}. The algorithm does not know p_i for any i.

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted causal bandit on no-backdoor graphs (cumulative regret)
unmapped: Arms are 2M+1 interventions on binary nodes plus observational arm in a no-backdoor causal graph
Observational arm reveals sampled values of all X_i (causal side information)
Interventions cost gamma>=1 (known), observation costs 1; budget B; regret against the best budget-feasible algorithm G_B
settings.definition_quote: Let G_ALG(B) be the expected reward accumulated by algorithm ALG with budget B, and let G_B = max_ALG G_ALG(B). Then, the cumulative regret of an algorithm ALG with budget B, denoted R_ALG(B), is R_ALG(B) = G_B - G_ALG(B)

settings.name_in_paper: Non-budgeted causal bandit on general graphs
unmapped: Learner knows the causal graph and the interventional parent distributions P(Pa(Y)=y | do(a)) for all arms a
Parent values Pa(Y) are observed each round; n parents each taking k values
All interventional parent distributions share the same non-zero support
settings.definition_quote: We assume the following: (a) the algorithm receives as input P(Pa(Y)= y| do(a)) for all a, and (b) the distributions P(Pa(Y)= y| do(a)) for all a have the same non-zero support.

symbols.M: number of intervenable binary nodes (2M+1 arms)

conditions: no backdoor paths from intervenable nodes to Y

source.label: theorem: simple regret observational algorithm
source.quote: The expected simple regret of \OBSALG with budget $B$ is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{1}{pB}\log (pMB)}\right)$.

results.notes: Proof assumes B >= some instance constant L. Bound independent of gamma since only observations are used.

symbols.gamma: cost ratio of intervention to observation

conditions: B sufficiently large (B >= max(gamma m, pM) and B >= (16/p^2) log terms, per proof)

source.label: theorem: simple regret of gammapba
source.quote: If $\gamma \geq \frac{1}{p\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}$ then the expected simple regret of \GammaPBA is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{1}{pB}\log (pMB)}\right)$, and if $\gamma \leq \frac{1}{p\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}$ then it is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\gamma\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}{B}\log \frac{MB}{\gamma \cdot m(\mathbf{p})}}\right)$.

symbols.gamma: cost ratio of intervention to observation
symbols.m_p: m(p) = min{tau : |I_tau| <= tau}, I_tau = {i : min_x p_{i,x} < 1/tau}

source.label: theorem: simple regret of gammapba
source.quote: if $\gamma \leq \frac{1}{p\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}$ then it is $O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\gamma\cdot m(\mathbf{p})}{B}\log \frac{MB}{\gamma \cdot m(\mathbf{p})}}\right)$.

bound.regime: a* = a_0 (observational arm optimal in cost-weighted sense)

source.label: theorem: cumulative regret of gamma paralllel bandit
source.quote: If $a^* = a_0$ then the expected cumulative regret of the algorithm is $O(1)$

results.notes: Proof gives 1 + 2M pi^2 (gamma-1)/3 + sum Delta_a pi^2/3. Regret is G_B - G_ALG(B) in expectation; mapped to pseudo_regret vs best feasible policy.

symbols.Delta_i: Delta_{i,x} = mu_{a*} - mu_{i,x} for interventional arm (i,x) (sum over those with Delta>0)

source.label: theorem: cumulative regret of gamma paralllel bandit
source.quote: otherwise the expected cumulative regret of the algorithm is of order $\sum_{\Delta_{i,x}>0} \Delta_{i,x}\left(\text{max}\left(0, 1+ 8\ln B\left(\frac{1}{d_{i,x}^2} - \frac{p_{i,x}}{3d_0^2}\right) \right) + \frac{\pi^2}{3}\right) + \Delta_0 \left(\frac{50\ln B}{d_{0}^2} + 1 + \frac{\pi^2}{3} \right)$.

results.notes: Theorem statement has p_{i,x}/(3 d_0^2) while proof derives p_{i,x}/(9 d_0^2); recorded as stated. 'of order' interpreted as O.

symbols.L_a: max{L_1, L_{2,a}}, L_1 = min{t : t >= 2 log(k^n t^2)/delta_c^2}, L_{2,a} = min{t : t >= 4 log(k^n t^2/2) zeta_a^2 / Delta_a^2}
symbols.k_vals: number of values each parent of Y takes

conditions: learner knows P(Pa(Y)=y|do(a)) for all a
all interventional parent distributions share the same nonzero support
unique optimal arm (assumed wlog in proof)

source.label: theorem: cumulative regret for general graphs
source.quote: Let $\delta = \min_{\mathbf{y}\in S^n} \{c_{\mathbf{y}} > 0\}$, $L_1 = ...$, $L_{2,a} = ...$, and $L_a = \text{max}\{L_1,L_{2,a}\}$. Then the expected cumulative regret of \CUCBTwo after $T$ rounds is at most $ \sum_{a\in \mathcal{A}} \Delta_a \Big(L_a + \frac{2\pi^2}{3}\Big).$

results.notes: Constant (T-independent) instance-dependent regret; algorithm does not need T. L_a depends on k^n and gaps (contains log terms in its definition).
